database systems  need users to understand database schemas and table relationships and query  syntax when they use Structured Query Language (SQL) to retrieve data from the  database. This method creates major difficulties for users who lack technical  knowledge because it requires them to spend more time and effort to find useful  information from complex databases that contain extensive data. The system  difficulties with manual query creation become exposed when data volume  increases and system complexity expands because users need simpler methods to  access database systems.<\/jats:p>\n                <jats:p>The system allows users  to express their data needs through natural language because it supports users  who want to access data without needing to learn SQL. A user can issue a  request by saying \"find risky users\" and the system will automatically  understand his request through its use of natural language processing and  artificial intelligence methods. The database system uses interpreted intent to  determine which schemas to use because it needs to comprehend data entity  relationships while creating optimized queries that produce accurate results  without user input during query development.<\/jats:p>\n                <jats:p>The introduction of  intent-based databases enables users to perform database operations through  natural language while the system handles schema selection and query  generation. The systems achieve their purpose by using contextual information  and security methods which verify that only permitted data is retrieved by  users. The deployment of intent-driven querying system provides users with an  efficient decision-making tool which can be easily scaled up to support future  database management
